answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by demanding proof of uniqueness from several independent trust domains at once: a government ID check, a bank KYC record, and a professional credential from unrelated authorities. Like saffron threads that gain value only when gathered from many flowers, an identity counts only when all domains agree it is the same real agent. A tide of fakes can flood one registry, but forging consistent records across timber-solid, independent issuers multiplies the attacker's cost, so mass fake identities become far costlier instead of nearly free.
